# the benchmark run behind docs/05-complexity-lab.md
#
# Regenerate with:  python -m tools.make_traces
# Do not edit by hand: tests/test_docs_traces.py compares this file with a
# fresh run of the code it shows.

## timings and element reads

Timings depend on the machine; the *shape* of the tables does not.  These
numbers were produced by `python -m tools.bench --sizes 125,250,500,1000`.
Reads are counted in a separate single run, so `repeat` does not inflate them.

### input shape: random(4 letters)

```
+-------------------------+------+-----------+-----------+-----------+----------------------------+
| implementation          |    n | positions |    slices | best of 3 | result                     |
+-------------------------+------+-----------+-----------+-----------+----------------------------+
| reference (O(n^3))      |  125 |         0 |   333,375 |  17.50 ms | length 6, 1 answer(s)      |
| reference (O(n^3))      |  250 |         0 | 2,635,500 | 132.98 ms | length 10, 1 answer(s)     |
| reference (O(n^3))      |  500 |         - |         - |         - | too slow to be useful here |
| reference (O(n^3))      | 1000 |         - |         - |         - | too slow to be useful here |
|                         |      |           |           |           |                            |
| brute_force             |  125 |       490 |        60 |  185.3 us | length 6, 1 answer(s)      |
| brute_force             |  250 |     1,027 |        76 |  390.9 us | length 10, 1 answer(s)     |
| brute_force             |  500 |     2,112 |        76 |  843.2 us | length 10, 1 answer(s)     |
| brute_force             | 1000 |     4,295 |        96 |   1.72 ms | length 10, 3 answer(s)     |
|                         |      |           |           |           |                            |

| brute_force_incremental |  500 |     2,112 |        76 |  412.4 us | length 10, 1 answer(s)     |
| brute_force_incremental | 1000 |     4,295 |        96 |  852.2 us | length 10, 3 answer(s)     |
|                         |      |           |           |           |                            |
```
